:: J U D G M E N T :
:

The Police Inspector of Subramanyanagar Police Station arising out of their Police Station crime in No.253/2015 filed charge sheet against the accused for his alleged commission of offences punishable under section 406, 408, 420 of IPC.
2.

The prosecution case in nutshell is that the accused was working as an Accounts Manager in the Sri C.C.No.13543/2016 Parijatha Hotels (BNG) Pvt. Ltd., situated at Dr.Rajakumar Road,
Rajajinagar Bengaluru.
The accused was entrusted with collection of amount from the customers and accounts.

But the accused during the period from 01.03.2015 to 06.10.2015 misappropriated an amount of Rs.12,62,494/ which had been collected from the customers and thereby the accused has committed the offences punishable under section 406, 408, 420 of IPC.
3. On the basis of Police report this court had taken cognizance of the aforesaid offences and registered the present case.
4. After service of summons the accused appeared before the court and obtained bail.
Having supplied to the prosecution papers to the accused and after heard both sides charge framed for the alleged commission of offences punishable under section 406, 408 and 420 of IPC.
Having understood the charges read over and explained by this court to the accused.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
The prosecution in order to prove its case examined one witness i.e., Sri.R.Govindaraju investigating officer as PW1 examined as PW1 against six witnesses cited in the charge sheet.
The prosecution has also relied upon Exs.
P1 to 14
documents.

Shaileshkumar vs Sudhakar Nayak @ Sudhakar on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37802983/
2 6.
Incriminating circumstance has appeared against the accused in the prosecution evidence read over and explained to him.
Having understood the same the accused has given his statement under section 313 of Cr.PC and same has been duly recorded by this court.
The accused did not choose to lead defence evidence.

7. Heard arguments on both side.
8.
The following points arise for court's consideration, POINTS 1.

Whether the prosecution beyond reasonable doubts proves that, the accused was working as Accounts Manager in Sri.Parijatha Hotels (BNG) Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru and he was entrusted with accounts section and C.C.No.13543/2016 collected the amount from the customers and the said amount credit to the Sri.Parijatha Hotels and the accused from 01.03.2015 to 06.10.2015 misappropriated an amount of Rs.12,62,494/ for his personal use and thereby he has committed criminal breach of trust thereby committed offences punishable under section 406, 408 of IPC.
2. Whether the prosecution, beyond reasonable doubt, proves that the accused was dishonestly induced an amount of Rs.12,62,494/ with an intention to cheat the Sri.Parijatha Hotels, Bengaluru and misappropriated by using the said amount for his personal use and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 420 of IPC.
3. What order?

9. The court's answer to the above points is as follows;
Point No.1 : In the Negative.
Point No.2 : In the Negative.
Point No.3 : As per final order.

C.C.No.13543/2016 REASONS 10. Point No.1 and 2: The PW1 registered this case on the basis of information given by the CW1 namely Sri.Shailesh Kumar S/o R.Prasad who was the General Manager of the Sri.Parijatha Hotels (BNG) Pvt. Ltd., Dr.Rajkumar Road, Bengaluru.

In the information he alleged that three employees namely Sudhakar Nayak Accounts Manager, Prabhu Duty Manager, Theertha Front Office Assistant,
were misappropriated an amount of Rs.15 lakhs from the March2015 to 06.10.2015.
On the basis of information the PW1 registered the FIR in Cr.No.253/2015 and investigated the matter and submitted the final report against the accused Sudhakar Nayak only.
The other two witnesses namely Prabhu and Theertha are not charge sheeted.

The prosecution case is that the accused was Accounts Manager, he was entrusted with collect the money from customers and credited the same to the account of Sri.Parijatha Hotels (BNG) Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru.
But the accused misappropriated an amount of Rs.12,62,494/ from 01.03.2015 to 06.10.2015.

Shaileshkumar vs Sudhakar Nayak @ Sudhakar on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37802983/
3 C.C.No.13543/2016 11.
The CW1 to 5 were the residents of Bengaluru among them CW1 to 4 are the employees of the Sri.Parijatha Hotels (BNG) Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru and CW5 was Chartered Accountant who issued audit report.
The Court made all its ventures to secure their presence.
In spite of issuance summons and warrants repeatedly it could not possible to secure them.
In spite of publication of proclamation they have not turned up.
Hence, this court dropped them.
The investigation officer CW6/PW1 deposed by narrating the manner in which, he conducted investigation.
It is to be noted that he collected no documentary evidence to show that the accused was working as Accounts Manager in Sri.Parijatha Hotels (BNG) Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru.
The PW1 registered the case as per Ex.P2 on the basis of Ex.P1 and conducted panchanama as per Ex.P3 and collected Ex.P4 to 14 documents.
Ex.P4 is the Letter issued by Sri.Parijatha Hotels (BNG) Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru to the investigation officer for production of audit report.
Ex.P5 is the Audit Report, wherein it is clearly shows that during period from 01.04.2015 to 06.10.2015 an amount of Rs.12,62,494/ C.C.No.13543/2016 short fall and not tallied.

The Chartered Accountant concluded that 'from the study of the records made available and the facts and circumstances under which this matter came to be verified, we are of the opinion that there are indications of a deliberate attempt made by the persons in charge of billing, cash collections and accounts, to mislead the management to show daily lower cash collections by inflating the credit card settlement amount'.
Ex.P6 is the Annexure1 which discloses that monthly details of misappropriation of cash.
These two documents clearly shows that during the period from 01.04.2015 to 06.10.2015 an amount of Rs.12,62,494/ was misappropriated by the person incharge of accounts.

12. Ex.P8 is the letter issued by Sri.Parijatha Hotels (BNG) Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru to investigation officer dated 12.12.2015, wherein they have stated that the appointment letter of accused was not available in their office.
It is further stated that the accused took the said letter.
In order to prove the entrustment the appointment letter is only not required.

The investigation officer could have collected other C.C.No.13543/2016 documents like original attendance book or accounts books which are having signature of accused, CCTV Footages or any other documents to show that he was working in the Sri.Parijatha Hotels (BNG) Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru as Accounts Manager.
But, the investigation officer has not made any efforts to collect those documents.

He has collected Ex.P9 which discloses one attendance of one Sudhakar Nayak but it is a photo copy and only on this document the court cannot come to the conclusion that the accused was entrusted with accounts section.
If produced said original document then it can be relied.

But in the absence of original attendance certificate or attendance book only on the basis of Ex.P9 document the court cannot come to the conclusion that the accused was entrusted with accounts section.
Ex.P10 to 13 are the Trade License Certificates of Sri.Parijatha Hotels (BNG) Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru.
Ex.P14 is the Appointment Letter of complainant.

The investigation officer recorded the statements of accused but as per section 25 of Indian Evidence Act the statement or confession statement alleged to have given by accused is not admissible as per law.

Even C.C.No.13543/2016 there is clear evidence of misappropriation of money by the person incharge of Accounts Manager, in the absence of entrustment accounts section to the accused, only on the basis of audit report the court cannot come to the conclusion that the accused was misappropriated the amount.

Shaileshkumar vs Sudhakar Nayak @ Sudhakar on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37802983/
4 13.

Absolutely, there is no convincing evidence to prove that the accused was entrusted with accounts manager and to collect the money from the customers and to remit the same to the Sri.Parijatha Hotels (BNG) Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru.
Even in the absence of evidence of CW1 to 5 the investigation officer could have proved the alleged offence of the accused by way of documentary evidence in respect of entrustment.
But no such documentary evidence having probative value and collected produced before this court.
Therefore, the accused is entitled for acquittal.
Hence, I answered Point No.1 and 2 in the Negative.
14. Point No.3:

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
C.C.No.13543/2016 ::ORDER::
In exercising the powers conferred under Section 248(1) of the Cr.P.C., the accused is hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under Section 406, 408 and 420 of IPC.
The accused is directed to comply the section 437(A) of Cr.PC.
His bail bonds stand cancelled.
(Dictated to the stenographer, transcribed by him on computer, corrected, then signed and pronounced by me in the open court on this the 13 th Day of March, 2024) (Shreyansh Doddamani)
III Addl., Chief Metropolitan Magistrate., Bengaluru.
